title: Swap Left and Right Everywhere

concept.title: Change the tree itself, and return its root
body: So far the functions only **read** the tree. This one **changes** it: every node swaps its left and right child. A recursive function can do it in the usual way: invert the left subtree, invert the right subtree, and swap the two results at the root.

body.code:
def invert(root):
    if root is None:
        return None
    left = invert(root.left)
    right = invert(root.right)
    root.left = right
    root.right = left
    return root                    # the same root, now with swapped children

body: Returning the root makes the function easy to use and also lets it handle the empty tree. The result is the **mirror image** of the tree. Remember: you modify the nodes that the starter code built, so the printed tree is the inverted one.

statement: Invert a binary tree: swap the left and right children of every node. Print the inverted tree in level order in the same form as the input (`N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
outputFormat: The inverted tree in level order on one line.
constraints: The height of a tree is at most 800.
hints: Swap the two children of every node.
Invert both subtrees first (or after), then swap.
Return the root so the caller can print the tree.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def invert(root):
    # Your code here
    return root

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()

print_tree(invert(build_tree(vals)))

explanation: Each call inverts its two subtrees and then stores them swapped, so every node ends up with its children exchanged.
